The Program Manager (Branch Manager for Field Services) in the Real Estate Management Division, Facilities and Administration, Mission Support, Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Duties include but are not limited to: Duties include: Provides overall leadership and supervision for the division, including planning, communicating vision and objectives, setting priorities, managing budget and resources, recruiting and developing staff, approving leave, and taking corrective/disciplinary actions.

Ensures workforce alignment with organizational goals and manages a multi-sector workforce. Leads, directs, and exercises broad authority over all phases of real estate management policies, strategic planning, and program operations for TSA.

Provides innovative leadership in establishing and implementing comprehensive real estate management strategies. Oversees activities related to TSA's leased and owned real estate portfolios, including lease acquisition, administration, facilities operations and maintenance, construction, and real estate disposition.

Supervises a team of Realty Services Managers (RSM) who direct, implement, coordinate, and oversee a national real estate program requiring a wide range of management support principles, processes and systems. The RSMs manage initiations and renewals of leases, which require a complex process of negotiations between and approvals by the parties.

Provides oversight and management direction for contracted functions, ensuring efficient and effective use of public and private resources in support of TSA's mission.

Implements policies and procedures to reduce TSA's real estate footprint through space consolidation and utilization, and operational costs by deploying energy efficiency tools, consistent with OMB guidance.

Collaborates with TSA office directors and interacts with senior leaders within TSA, DHS, GSA, and service providers to ensure operational facility requirements are prudently executed and managed.

Administers a diverse, enterprise-wide real estate portfolio, ensuring full compliance with federal leasing regulations, lease expirations, and portfolio performance metrics. Manages and executes over 500 GSA leases, ensuring terms are negotiated in the best financial interest of the agency.

Navigates the GSA Reimbursable Work Authorization process, ensuring accurate funding data, budget tracking, and timely execution of tenant improvement projects. Provides proactive, outstanding customer service and real estate solutions to field real estate locations, addressing space requirements and facility concerns and improvements.

Conducts special real estate projects and complex analyses, as assigned by the Director, requiring a comprehensive knowledge of program management. Supervisory/Managerial duties includes serving as a first line supervisor for the organization.

This includes but is not limited to: assigning work, setting priorities, and reviewing and evaluating work and performance of subordinates; approving leave; coaching and developing employees; recommending corrective or disciplinary actions; assisting in budget planning and projecting short-term needs; managing projects within assigned resources; resolving routine problems that typically impact the objectives of the organizational unit; and when required, coordinating with customers outside the immediate organization.
To qualify for the SV-K Pay Band (equivalent to GS-15), you must have one year of specialized experience at the SV-J or GS-14 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector.

Specialized experience is defined as experience that has equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Specialized experience is defined as: Knowledge of federal laws, regulations, policies, and procedures related to real estate management, leasing, facilities operations, and asset disposition. Experience in managing multi-layered, geographically dispersed organizations with varied missions and functional requirements.

Credit for experience is given based on a 40-hour workweek. Part-time experience is credited on a part-time ratio, i.e., working 20 hours per week for two months equals one month of experience. No additional credit is given for overtime.

National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees.

If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office.

Resumes must include the following: Narrative description of duties with start and end dates (including the month and year) for work experience. State the number of hours worked in a position (i.e. full-time or part-time). If part-time, state the total number of hours worked per week.

Performance level (i.e. band or grade) You must meet the qualification requirements for this position no later than the closing date of the vacancy announcement.

You will manage assigned projects, define project scope and tasks; identify task details and interfaces between tasks.
You will serve as lead to coordinate activities related to applications and projects.
You will maintain portfolios for assigned projects including milestones, risk assessments, interfaces, and funding requirements.
You will serve as the primary customer liaison for the IPT, ensuring that user requirements and feedback are continuously integrated into project planning to meet both customer expectations and corporate business goals.
You will actively engage with customers to identify emerging operational needs, collaboratively reviewing new initiatives and technology trends to ensure our solutions directly enhance customer capabilities and satisfaction.
You will partner with diverse user groups to conduct needs assessments, utilizing direct customer feedback and feasibility studies to drive project modifications that maximize user adoption and mission readiness.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1.) Designing, configuring, deploying, or managing Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software solutions (such as Siemens Teamcenter) to support engineering, configuration management, or product data workflows. 2.) Managing, developing, or maintaining complex IT systems, networks, or security architectures. 3.) Resolving critical technical issues and advising leadership on strategic IT integrations. 4.) Planning and executing major IT projects, ensuring compliance with organizational standards. 5.) Providing technical guidance, instruction, and peer training to team members. 6.) Monitoring progress and reporting accomplishments or obstacles to the supervisor Your experience must reflect skill in the following areas: attention to detail, customer service, oral communication, and problem solving.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

The duties and responsibilities for a IT Project Manager (NETWORK/INFOSEC) GS-2210-13 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Monitor infrastructure performance, availability, reliability, resiliency, operational readiness, and service dependencies; resolve complex operational issues.

Coordinate with budget, acquisition, contracting, program, and technical personnel to ensure effective management of IT resources. Develop network project plans, technical requirements, implementation strategies, schedules, milestones, and resource requirements.

Provide technical recommendations to contracting officials regarding contract administration, modifications, deliverable acceptance, schedule changes, and performance issues. Lead cross-functional teams of technical staff, program officials, contractors, vendors, and internal/external stakeholders.
To qualify for the position of IT Project Manager (NETWORK/INFOSEC), at GS-2210-13, you must meet the basic qualification requirements listed below. Basic Qualifications (2210 series): Please refer to the OPM IT Management Series 2210 Qualification Standard for the specific experience requirements for the GS-12 and above positions.

AND Specialized Experience: To qualify for the GS-13 grade level, you must have one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service, or comparable non-Federal experience.

Specialized experience is defined as experience performing the following duties: Participate in the planning execution and monitoring enterprise IT projects involving network services, information security, and/or telecommunications. You MUST meet all qualification requirements by the 09/04/2026 of this announcement.

Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating. See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume.

After you submit this application, you will receive an e-mail informing you that a USA Hire assessment is required of you. You will have 48 hours from the closing date of this announcement 09/04/2026 to complete the assessment as this assessment is part of your application.

The purpose of the Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI) Program Manager is to provide independent clinical administration of the Primary Care Mental Health program and supervision of interdisciplinary staff who work in the Program.

Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional Duties include, but are not limited to: The incumbent carries out the following supervisory authorities and responsibilities: Provides direct line supervision of an interdisciplinary team of PCMHI staff, including social workers, psychologists, and prescribing providers, with anticipation of program expansion.

Plans work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules for completion of work. Assigns work to subordinates based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees. Evaluates work performance of subordinates.

Coordinating services offered to veterans and their families enrolled in the program. Services include functional assessment, medications, crisis intervention, educational, individual, and group treatment, interventions specific to chronic health conditions, and care management.

Formulating, interpreting, and implementing policies and procedures pertaining to quality mental health care in PCMHI to assure compliance with internal and external performance standards. Developing effective programs and treatment strategies for PCMHI program patients.

Interfacing with other program Managers, Service Chief, Mental Health product line leadership, and VA personnel. Advising Mental Health leadership on relevant programmatic issues with recommendations for improvement in service delivery. Collaborating with other program directors and managers as a member of the Mental Health Executive Committee.

Collaborating with Primary Care executive staff as a member of the PACT Steering Committee. Maintaining effective working relationship with internal and external customer groups. Adhering to the requirements of the Master Agreement between the Department of Veterans Affairs and the American Federation of Government Employees.

The program manager will provide PCMHI-consistent care to patients within the PCMHI clinic.

This may include engaging patients through alternative technologies (e.g., telehealth, CVT to home) Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8:00am-4:30pm (subject to change based on facility needs) Recruitment Incentive (Sign-on Bonus): Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (Relocation Assistance): Not Authorized EDRP Authorized: Former EDRP participants ineligible to apply for incentive.

Contact raja.kadeem@va.gov, the EDRP Coordinator for questions/assistance. Learn more Pay: Competitive salary and regular salary increases. When setting pay, a higher step rate of the appropriate grade may be determined after consideration of higher or unique qualifications or special needs of the VA (Above Minimum Rate of the Grade).

Paid Time Off: 37-50 days of annual paid time offer per year (13-26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year)Selected applicants may qualify for credit toward annual leave accrual, based on prior work experience or military service experience.

Parental Leave: After 12 months of employment, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave in connection with the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child.

Child Care Subsidy: After 60 days of employment, full time employees with a total family income below $144,000 may be eligible for a childcare subsidy up to 25% of total eligible childcare costs for eligible children up to the monthly maximum of $416.66.

Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Functional Statement #: 00999F Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorize
Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship. Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education. Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re- specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re- specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: (a) The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, (b) the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature. AND Internships.

Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96- 151 (pre- 1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally- accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one- year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program. Licensure.

Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). Grade Determinations: Psychology Program Manager, GS-14 Experience.

At least three years of experience as a professional psychologist, with at least one year equivalent to the GS-13 grade level. Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities.

In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: Ability to organize work, set priorities, delegate tasks, and meet multiple deadlines. Knowledge of and ability to utilize evidence based practices and clinical practice guidelines appropriately and ability to guide staff in using these tools.

Ability to deal effectively with individuals or groups. Skill in managing and directing the work of others to accomplish program goals and objectives. Ability to translate management goals and objectives into well-coordinated and controlled work operations. Ability to establish and monitor production and performance priorities and standards.

Ability to analyze organizational and operational problems and to develop and implement solutions that result in sound operation of the program. Preferred Experience: PCMHI experience, supervisory experience. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-14. Physical Requirements: Physical aspects associated with work required of this assignment are typical for the occupation, see Duties section for essential job duties of the position. May require standing, lifting, carrying, sitting, stooping, bending, puling, and pushing.

May be required to wear personal protective equipment and undergo annual TB screening or testing as conditions of employment. Work Environment: Work is performed in an office/clinic setting with minimal risks that requires normal safety precautions; the area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated.

However, the work environment requires someone with the ability to handle several tasks at once in sometimes stressful situations.

The United States Space Force (USSF) at Buckley Space Force Base, Colorado is searching for a Resource Adviser & Program Manager to support the 11 SWS (NH-0301-02, GS 05-11 equivalent). Description: Administrative Management): Directly assists the commander/director in the management of all administrative support program functions.

Administers programs and serves as the primary source of information. The incumbent is responsible for the preparation, maintenance, and deposition of required administrative reports and other correspondence.

Assists commander/director in accomplishing all necessary internal operations to include administrative training, security, development of organizational operating instructions and regulations, and personnel assistance.

Acts as the point of contact for all newly assigned personnel; orients them regarding the basic functions of the organization, introduces them to key personnel and schedules their initial training/orientation requirements Program Compliance & Management): Serves as the resident subject matter expert for all mandated administrative support programs.

Ensures unit program compliance with regulations, laws, policies, and squadron commander directives.

Responsible for programs to include but not limited to task management, cybersecurity liaison (CL), Government Travel Card (GTC) program, Unit Deployment Manager (UDM), Defense Travel System (DTS) administrator, drug demand reduction program, health care program, fitness program, Government Purchase Card (GPC) program, safety program, Automated Data Processing Equipment (ADPE) accounts, security program, supply program, civilian timecard program and unit recognition program.

Develops and implements procedures to track program status and maintain program health. Serves as the organizational point of contact and liaison with the personnel flight on military and civilian personnel issues.

Stays abreast of current personnel issues and provides explanations of personnel-related requirements, regulations, and procedures to supervisors and managers. Determines the necessary steps to perform the full range of administrative functions associated with personnel assignments, promotions, and performance evaluations.

Generates and processes required military and civilian personnel transactions. Monitors military personnel action requests, tracks personnel, manpower, and training transactions as documentation flows through the office and provides status reports to management.

Monitors preparation of performance reports, reviews for accuracy and consistency with available guidelines, and ensures timely submission. Coordinates work efforts affecting organizational personnel with appropriate offices and resolves conflicts. Assists in planning, administering, and monitoring manpower resource requirements.

Serves as the point of contact for both civilian and military position utilization. Maintains manpower manning documents. Reviews requests for revised manpower authorizations, and makes recommendations for approval or disapproval as required. Receives changes to UMD and notifies appropriate officials and follows up with appropriate action.

Provides guidance to supervisors relating to military and civilian manpower requirements, organizational structure, authorization and utilization of positions, military civilian mix, skills imbalance. Reviews requests for military and civilian fills. Reviews requests for civilian over hires. Reviews all projected movements of authorizations.

Performs other clerical and administrative work in support of the office/organization. Develops, establishes, updates, and maintains office procedures and records/files of various types to ensure effective and efficient operation of the office.

Provides advice and guidance to staff in the organization on administrative, clerical, and procedural requirements. Assists other clerical staff in locating and selecting the appropriate guidelines, references, and procedures for application to specific cases. Updates tracker or suspense files for unclassified documents as required.

In accordance with established procedures prepares, consolidates, submits, and maintains time and attendance. Assists project officer in making arrangements for command sponsored events ensuring proper protocol is followed. Advises the installation commander on all budgetary, financial, and resource management matters.

Executes the commander's vision on resource allocation in support of mission and installation operations, maintenance, and sustainment. Performs budget formulation work, including the preparation of detailed analyses of annual and/or multi-year budget estimates for assigned organizations/programs into a consolidated budget request.

Assembles and/or develops background data, information, and documentation to support required program budgets.

About Phase2 Our remote first employees join and stay at Phase2 to be a force . In pursuit of digital experience that advances the human experience, you will do your best work, live fully, and succeed as a team.

Phase2 a digital agency passionate about customer experience, grounded in data & insights, and rooted in more than two decades of successful technology delivery. We guide industry-leading companies to what’s next in their digital slandscape. And it all begins with finding the right people who align with our values and passion for impact.

About the Role Phase2 is seeking a Senior Project Manager to own complex digital engagements and lead trusted, senior-level client relationships. Project managers often focus on the triple constraint of scope, time, and cost, but Phase2 is seeking a different breed of PM who can think beyond constraints.

Project Managers at Phase2 create a unique, engaging, and impactful client experience with long-term outcomes. They bring a future-focused perspective, anticipate client needs, and ensure decisions and direction align with what will drive meaningful progress and outcomes.

They bring clarity to ambiguity, guide clients through key decisions, and keep work moving forward, ensuring clients feel confident, supported, and satisfied.

This position reports to: VP, Project Management Compensation: Base annual salary of $120,000 - $155,000 What You’ll Do Own multi-workstream engagements end-to-end, ensuring delivery stays aligned with client goals, expected outcomes, and organizational standards.

Set direction by translating client objectives into structured plans, decision frameworks, and actionable priorities. Drive outcomes and client value with an emphasis on rapid time to value, using practical delivery discipline and AI-enabled approaches to accelerate insight, execution, and impact.

Lead the client relationship with confidence and clarity, ensuring expectations are understood, risks and mitigations are discussed early, and decisions continue moving forward. Direct cross-functional teams by establishing clear and outcome-aligned workflows, communication patterns, and accountability across all contributors.

Take ownership of engagement financials, including scope, forecasting, staffing, and margin performance, adjusting plans as conditions shift. Own and evolve the engagement roadmap and delivery approach ensuring work is sequenced to drive momentum, demonstrate value early, and unlock what’s next.

Embed AI tools into engagement workflows to strengthen planning, insight generation, communication, and decision support—setting expectations for how teams use AI to improve clarity, efficiency, and quality of work. Provide grounded recommendations that help clients evaluate tradeoffs, understand implications, and make informed decisions.

Identify risks early, lead mitigation efforts, and ensure issues are resolved with clarity and speed. Recognize and shape opportunities that arise naturally from delivery insight, client context, or emerging needs. Support the creation of proposals, estimates, and scopes that reflect realistic delivery plans and forward-looking client priorities.

What You’ll Need Significant experience owning complex digital engagements and leading senior client relationships. A strong instinct for bringing order to complexity—setting direction, aligning teams, and maintaining steady progress across multiple workstreams.

Demonstrated ability to solve problems creatively and constructively, balancing constraints across scope, budget, timelines, and team capacity without compromising outcomes. Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to lead client discussions, present recommendations, and guide decisions.

Deep understanding of digital platforms, product development lifecycles, and modern delivery practices. Demonstrated ability to embed AI in daily workflows and deliverables—using it to accelerate analysis, sharpen communication, synthesize information, and elevate the overall quality of engagement leadership.

Experience guiding teams in responsible, effective AI use, ensuring it enhances outcomes, improves speed and structure, and supports stronger decision-making. A track record of identifying meaningful opportunities rooted in client strategy, delivery insight, or future potential. Agency or consultancy experience preferred.

What Success Looks Like Clients feel led, supported, and confident in both the direction and decisions of the engagement. Teams operate with clarity, alignment, and consistent direction, even as priorities evolve. Engagements maintain predictable delivery, proactive risk management, and stable momentum.

Decisions are shaped with context, structure, and clear implications, enabling clients to move forward confidently. Clients feel energized and inspired by the clarity, momentum, and possibilities the partnership creates. New opportunities emerge naturally because the work is thoughtful, high-performing, and forward-looking.

Engagements meet expectations across delivery quality, relationship strength, and commercial performance. What You’ll Get The chance to make a real impact in the health and wellness space, helping millions of people per year. To work from wherever you thrive best. We’re a remote-first team built on trust, flexibility, and outcomes.

A competitive compensation package that considers various factors. A comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage, and supplemental insurance. Our fun and interactive wellness program offers rewards for participation.

A 401(k) with a 3% employer contribution–no match required and 100% vested after just 90 days. You’ll start with 16 paid vacation days, 4 personal days, and 1 volunteer day each year. Vacation and personal time increase with your tenure, recognizing your continued contributions.

Up to 12 weeks of fully paid leave for birthing parents and up to 6 weeks of fully paid bonding leave, based on your tenure. This includes support for adoption and foster placement, along with the option to extend time off through additional unpaid leave.

Inclusive fertility, adoption, and surrogacy benefits through Kindbody, along with virtual health coaching and care navigation. A $500 stipend to personalize and equip your home workspace for success. What the Environment Looks Like Physical Demands Frequently remain in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods of time.

Occasional adjusting or moving of light objects up to 20 pounds in all directions. Continuous communication on live video chats, calls, and through emails and messaging platforms for the purpose of exchanging information. Continuous repetitive movements that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers. Travel, sometimes frequent, is expected.

Mental Demands Comprehension - Must continuously be able to understand direction and adhere to established procedures. Must also be able to gather information from clients and employees and synthesize this information in a meaningful way. May also be responsible for making improvements or recommendations to existing procedures.

Organization - Must continuously be able to gather and classify information, store information learned from conversations and communications, and then be and be able to quickly recall, interpret, and explain information. Reasoning and Decision Making - Must continuously use logic to analyze and interpret information, and prioritize.

Communication - Must continuously express or exchange ideas and meaning with employees and clients. Resilience - Must continuously adapt well in the face of workplace stressors. Klub44 ist ein gemeinnütziges Startup im Bereich digitale Jugendbeteiligung. Mit der Klub-App ermöglichen wir es jungen Menschen, ihre eigene Stadt und ihre Vorlieben zu entdecken, und die Welt um sich herum mitzugestalten. Alle jungen Menschen haben das Recht auf ein freies und schöpferisches Leben, daran glauben wir fest.
Nebenbei möchten wir die Schul- und Berufsbildung radikal transformieren.
Mit der Klub-App erhalten Jugendliche ab 12 Jahren einen chancengerechten Zugang zu kostenfreien Freizeit- und Berufsorientierungsangeboten. Außerschulische Standorte – z. B. Jugendclubs, Makerspaces, Orte der kulturellen Bildung – können auf unserer App ihre Angebote direkt und digital an Jugendliche kommunizieren. Das Ganze bauen wir als Game auf: Entdecke deine Stadt, dich selbst, und bekomme dafür Rewards!
Wir ermutigen ausdrücklich Menschen aller Geschlechter, Religionen und sexuellen Orientierungen dazu, sich bei uns zu bewerben!
Aufgaben
Als Projektmanager*in Kooperationen bist du die Person, bei der unsere operativen Projekte zusammenlaufen. Kommunen, Schulen und Stiftungen arbeiten mit uns, weil sie ein Ergebnis wollen – du sorgst dafür, dass dieses Ergebnis auch eintritt: im Zeitplan, im Budget, und mit zufriedenen Partnern.

Gleichzeitig hast du einen zweiten Auftrag, der genauso wichtig ist: Du führst so viele Projekte wie möglich über unsere Standardprozesse, damit Klub als Plattform skalierbar bleibt und nicht in Sonderlösungen erstickt. Diese Doppelrolle – nach außen verbindlich, nach innen konsequent – ist der Kern des Jobs.
Wir freuen uns auf Mitunternehmer*innen, um gemeinsam mit dem jungen Team und Geschäftsführer Sebastian die Geschicke von Klub44 zu leiten.
Projektsteuerung
Eigenverantwortliche Steuerung unserer laufenden Kooperationsprojekte – von Kick-off bis Abschluss.
Planung von Meilensteinen, Verantwortlichkeiten und Terminen; Nachhalten, wenn es hakt.
Frühzeitiges Erkennen von Risiken und aktives Gegensteuern, statt Überraschungen am Projektende.
Sicherstellen, dass zugesagte Ziele (z. B. teilnehmende Standorte, aktive Jugendliche, Angebots-Uploads) tatsächlich erreicht werden.
Account Management & Partnerbetreuung
Du bist die verlässliche Ansprechperson für unsere Projektpartner in Kommunen, Schulen und Stiftungen – die Stimme von Klub im Alltag.
Aufbau langfristiger Beziehungen: Bestehende Kooperationen erfolgreich umsetzen, verlängern und ausbauen.
Erwartungsmanagement mit Verwaltungen, Schulleitungen und Förderpartnern: klar sagen, was geht, und was nicht.
Übersetzungsarbeit zwischen kommunaler Logik und Startup-Tempo – in beide Richtungen.
Skalierbarkeit & Standardprozesse
Onboarding von Kommunen, Schulen und Jugendeinrichtungen entlang unserer Standardprozesse – wiederholbar statt jedes Mal neu.
Weiterentwicklung dieser Prozesse: Playbooks, Templates, Checklisten, Automatisierungen.
Erkennen, wann eine Partneranfrage ein Sonderfall ist – und wann sie in ein neues Standardangebot gehört.
Bewusstes Nein zu Individuallösungen, die uns langfristig teuer werden.
Zahlen, Reporting & Wirkung
Nachhalten der Projekt-KPIs und transparentes internes Reporting zum Projektstatus.
Aufbereitung von Projektständen und Wirkungsdaten für Zuwendungsgeber und Stiftungen – die Verantwortung für Verwendungsnachweise und Reportings liegt bei der Geschäftsführung, du lieferst die Grundlage.
Ableiten konkreter Maßnahmen aus den Zahlen, nicht nur Dokumentation.
Zusammenarbeit im Team
Enge Abstimmung mit Geschäftsführung, Marketing & Community und Produktentwicklung.
Rückkopplung von Partner-Feedback ins Produkt: Was brauchen Kommunen und Standorte wirklich?
Steuerung externer Partner und Dienstleister im Projektkontext.
Qualifikation
Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung im Projektmanagement und bringst Projekte nachweislich zum Abschluss – idealerweise mit Partnern aus Verwaltung, Bildung, Stiftungen oder NGOs. Arbeitserfahrung in einem Startup ist ein guter Bonus.
Du bist stark in Kooperation und Kommunikation: Du gewinnst Menschen für gemeinsame Ziele und behältst dabei die Interessen von Klub im Blick.
Du denkst in Prozessen und Systemen, nicht in Einzelfällen – und hast Freude daran, Wiederholbares zu bauen.
Du arbeitest strukturiert und verbindlich: Zusagen, Fristen und Follow-ups sitzen bei dir.
Du bist "hands on" und sicher im Umgang mit agilen Methoden und Projektmanagement-Tools.
Du arbeitest datenbasiert und bist sicher im Nachhalten von Kennzahlen.
Dich motivieren unternehmerische Herausforderungen und du möchtest persönlich dazu beitragen, Jugendliche bei einer chancengerechten Entfaltung ihrer Potenziale zu fördern.
Du hast sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und verhandlungssichere Englischkenntnisse.
Als junges, gemeinnütziges Startup sind wir noch limitiert, wollen aber mittelfristig marktgerecht zahlen. Bis wir das hinkriegen, können wir auch kreativ sein.

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re-specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re-specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.

Internship Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96-151 (pre-1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

Licensure: Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

English Language Proficiency: Psychologists must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section A, paragraph 3j.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria).

As a Supervisory Program Manager, you will: Serve as a principal advisor and consultant to the Associate Administrator, and as appropriate the Administrator and Deputy Administrator on all activities related to FTA to improve public transportation research programs and projects.

Prepare resource allocation plans and implement research strategies for designated programs; conduct analysis of established practices and procedures; review and evaluate the effectiveness of designated research programs and initiatives in relation to the agency's mission, functions, and programs.

Provide guidance on transit a grant programs; review, analyze, and make recommendations on national issues relevant to grant programs.

Advise the Associate Administrator on the strategic planning, allocation, and oversight of FTA research funds, including the annual spend plan, research portfolio management, including reports and data, and development of a comprehensive research strategy for FTA and the transit industry.

Provide direction pertaining to the human and physical resources of TRI; including workforce planning, employee performance, recruitment, promotions, awards, administrative actions, and allocation of equipment, facilities, and other resources.

The Ideal Candidate will have proven experience independently supporting or playing a key role in program analysis projects at the office or division level, with a focus on evaluating operational workflows and utilizing data to generate actionable programmatic reports.

The candidate must have hands-on experience evaluating, drafting, and documenting standard operating procedures (SOPs) or localized business processes to support daily programmatic or operational needs.

Direct experience coordinating, gathering, and documenting business and operational requirements aimed at supporting, improving, or implementing localized non-IT or business-side programmatic processes is an asset.
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.

Experience managing the planning, budget, technical and financial aspects of multi-year programs. Experience managing an environment with multiple and competing priorities that require the application of strategic determinations, collaborative decision making, emotional intelligence, and strong written and oral communication abilities.

Planning and Evaluating - Organizes work, sets priorities, and determines resource requirements; determines short- or long-term goals and strategies to achieve them; coordinates with other organizations or parts of the organization to accomplish goals; monitors progress and evaluates outcomes.

Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations; is sensitive to cultural diversity, race, gender, disabilities, and other individual differences.

Leadership - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations.

Sie treten standhaft, reflektiert und überzeugend auf, hinterfragen Anliegen und Erwartungen konstruktiv und vertreten auch weniger populäre, aber betriebsnotwendige Entscheide mit Augenmass und Klarheit

The Program Manager plays a critical role in driving the successful execution of strategic product initiatives across the organization. This role serves as the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Design, Operations, and Go-to-Market teams, ensuring alignment from strategy through delivery.

The ideal candidate combines strong program management expertise with a background in product management and engineering, enabling them to navigate technical complexity, influence decision-making, and accelerate business outcomes.

s.h: What you’ll do & how you’ll make your mark.
s.t:
Product & Program Leadership
Lead complex, cross-functional product and technology initiatives from concept through launch and adoption
Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to translate business objectives into executable plans and measurable outcomes
Drive alignment across stakeholders, balancing customer needs, technical constraints, and business priorities
Help define and operationalize processes that improve product development velocity and predictability
Strategic Planning & Roadmap Execution

Ensure dependencies, resource needs, risks, and trade-offs are identified and addressed proactively

Cross-Functional Delivery

Technical Program Management

Facilitate discussions involving system design, technical debt, scalability, reliability, and platform modernization

Translate complex technical concepts into clear business context for executive and non-technical stakeholders
Stakeholder Communication & Reporting
Build executive-level visibility into program health, roadmap progress, risks, and key decisions
Develop concise status updates, business reviews, and leadership presentations
Drive governance processes and decision-making frameworks for strategic initiatives
Proactively escalate risks and provide actionable recommendations
Process, Tools & Continuous Improvement
Own and maintain program artifacts, roadmaps, project plans, and documentation within Jira and Confluence
Establish and enforce best practices for work management, sprint planning, dependency tracking, reporting, and documentation across Product and Engineering teams
Develop dashboards, reports, and workflow processes that provide visibility into roadmap progress, delivery health, and team performance

This person does more than manage a project plan. They understand the technical work being performed, can follow the details of architecture and engineering conversations, recognize dependencies and delivery risks, and ensure the team is following HIKE2’s technical and project delivery playbooks.
The Technical Project Manager reports into the PMO and partners closely with Databricks architects, data engineers, technical leads, consultants, and client stakeholders.

Own the day-to-day execution and operating rhythm of assigned Databricks and data projects.
Own the connection between technical delivery, client priorities, and the business outcomes the platform is intended to enable.
Maintain the Jira board as the source of truth for project execution, including backlog, stories, tasks, dependencies, blockers, owners, and status.
Ensure work is appropriately defined, prioritized, assigned, estimated, and progressing through the delivery lifecycle.
Run project ceremonies including stand-ups, planning, backlog reviews, status meetings, and retrospectives as appropriate.
Produce and distribute the Weekly Pulse Report , clearly communicating progress, accomplishments, upcoming work, risks, decisions, dependencies, budget/burn, and items requiring attention.
Maintain project plans, milestones, RAID logs, decisions, action items, resource plans, and other required PMO artifacts.
Understand the technical delivery plan and ensure the team is following the established Databricks/data technical playbook .
Track technical dependencies across data sources, environments, pipelines, integrations, architecture, security, testing, deployment, and client teams.
Identify delivery risks early and drive issues to resolution rather than simply reporting status.
Ensure client and HIKE2 stakeholders have clear visibility into project health, decisions, risks, and next steps.
Partner with technical leads to translate technical work into an executable project plan and clear client communication.
Escalate issues through the PMO and delivery leadership when additional support or decisions are required

Cloud data environments

Development, testing, deployment, and environment management

Technical dependencies and integration points
Agile technical delivery and engineering backlogs

Notre bureau
Conti \& Associés Ingénieurs SA est un bureau d’ingénieurs spécialisé dans les techniques du bâtiment CVSER, implanté à Versoix (Genève) et Perroy (Vaud).
Actifs depuis 1983, nous regroupons aujourd’hui plus de 35 collaborateurs et intervenons dans les domaines suivants :

· Chauffage, ventilation et climatisation (CVC)

· Sanitaire

· Électricité

· Régulation / MCR et automatisme du bâtiment
Nous accompagnons nos clients sur l’ensemble des phases SIA 108, avec une activité importante sur les phases 3, 4 et 5 : études, appels d’offres, réalisation et réception des ouvrages. Nous intervenons également en phase 6 pour le suivi de l’exploitation et l’optimisation énergétique des bâtiments.
Notre activité couvre aussi les audits et diagnostics énergétiques, la physique du bâtiment, les études de faisabilité CVSER, les CECB\+, les missions GED et AMOén dans le cadre du programme éco21, ainsi que les expertises techniques CVSER pour des assurances, maîtres d’ouvrage ou dans le cadre de procédures judiciaires.

a/ Concevoir et dimensionner les installations sanitaires conformément aux normes, directives et règles de l’art applicables en Suisse.
b/ Réaliser les études des réseaux d’eau froide, eau chaude sanitaire, bouclage, eaux usées et eaux pluviales.
c/ Réaliser les calculs et dimensionnements nécessaires aux projets.
d/ Élaborer les plans, schémas de principe et détails techniques.
2/ Plans et soumissions
a/ Réaliser et mettre à jour les plans sanitaires sous AutoCAD 2D.
b/ Établir les quantitatifs et métrés nécessaires aux appels d’offres.
c/ Participer à l’élaboration des soumissions CAN à l’aide des outils spécifiques tels que Plancal Nova / SNAP.
d/ Participer à l’analyse technique des offres des entreprises.
3/ Coordination et réalisation
a/ Assurer la coordination technique avec les disciplines chauffage, ventilation, électricité et régulation.
b/ Participer aux séances avec les maîtres d’ouvrage, architectes, entreprises et autres mandataires.
c/ Participer au suivi de l’exécution des installations sur le terrain.
d/ Contrôler la conformité des installations avec les plans, normes et prescriptions du projet.
e/ Participer aux réceptions des installations et au suivi des réserves.
Votre profil

a/ CFC de projeteur(se) en technique du bâtiment sanitaire, technicien(ne) ES, maîtrise fédérale ou formation jugée équivalente.
b/ Expérience de plusieurs années dans un bureau d’ingénieurs, bureau d'études ou une entreprise sanitaire.
c/ Une expérience professionnelle en Suisse constitue un avantage important.
2/ Compétences techniques
a/ Bonne maîtrise d’AutoCAD 2D.
b/ Connaissance de Plancal Nova / SNAP et des soumissions selon le CAN sanitaire.
c/ Bonne connaissance des normes et prescriptions sanitaires suisses.
d/ Connaissance des prescriptions SSIGE et des directives techniques Geberit.
e/ La maîtrise de Revit / BIM constitue un atout.
f/ Bonne maîtrise des outils MS Office.

Du hast bereits in einer Agentur gearbeitet , behältst auch bei mehreren parallelen Kundenprojekten den Überblick und fühlst dich zwischen Kundenmeeting, Contentproduktion und Projektplanung wohl?
Dann suchen wir dich als Projektmanager (m/w/d) für unser Team bei wirdenkenlokal .
Wir sind Medienhaus und Agentur mit Sitz in Nürnberg und unterstützen Unternehmen dabei, sichtbar zu werden , neue Kunden zu erreichen und passende Mitarbeitende zu gewinnen . Dafür entwickeln und realisieren wir Projekte rund um Social Media, Video- und Fotoproduktion, Onlinekampagnen, PR und Events .
Für die Steuerung unserer Kundenprojekte suchen wir jemanden, der Verantwortung übernimmt , strukturiert arbeitet und gleichzeitig versteht, dass Agenturalltag nicht immer nach Lehrbuch läuft.
Aufgaben
Projektmanagement: Du übernimmst die eigenständige Steuerung unserer Agenturprojekte – von der Planung über die Koordination der Umsetzung bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss. Dabei betreust du Social-Media-Projekte, Videoproduktionen, Fotoshootings und weitere Online-Marketing-Kampagnen.
Kundenbetreuung & Beratung: Du bist eine zentrale Ansprechperson für unsere Kunden, führst regelmäßige Kundentermine und berätst sie entlang unseres Leistungsportfolios. Du verstehst, was der Kunde erreichen möchte, übersetzt Anforderungen in konkrete Aufgaben und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Team passende Lösungen.
Koordination & Überblick: Mehrere Kunden, unterschiedliche Deadlines und verschiedene interne Ansprechpartner gleichzeitig? Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel. Du priorisierst Aufgaben, koordinierst Timings und Ressourcen und sorgst dafür, dass alle Beteiligten wissen, was wann zu tun ist.
Contentproduktionen: Du bist nicht nur am Schreibtisch: Bei ausgewählten Video- und Fotoproduktionen unterstützt du unser Team vor Ort, koordinierst Abläufe und stellst gemeinsam mit unseren Kreativen sicher, dass die Anforderungen des Kunden umgesetzt werden.
Schnittstelle zwischen Kunde und Team: Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Social-Media-Managern, Videografen, Fotografen und weiteren Kolleginnen und Kollegen zusammen. Informationen, Feedback und Freigaben laufen bei dir zusammen und werden von dir strukturiert weitergegeben.
Projektmanagement mit Awork: Wir organisieren unsere Projekte mit Awork. Du musst das Tool noch nicht kennen – Erfahrung mit Projektmanagement-Tools wie Awork, Asana, Monday, Trello oder vergleichbaren Lösungen setzen wir allerdings voraus.
KI & Prozessoptimierung: Wir nutzen KI bereits intensiv in unserem Arbeitsalltag und wollen das weiter ausbauen. Du bist offen dafür, KI-Tools sowohl innerhalb von Kundenprojekten als auch zur Optimierung unserer internen Prozesse einzusetzen, neue Möglichkeiten auszuprobieren und bestehende Abläufe kontinuierlich besser zu machen.
Qualifikation
Agenturerfahrung: Du hast bereits in einer Marketing-, Social-Media-, Digital-, Content- oder vergleichbaren Agentur gearbeitet und kennst die Dynamik des Agenturalltags.
Erfahrung im Online-Marketing: Du bringst praktische Vorerfahrung und ein gutes Verständnis für Social Media, Contentproduktion und Onlinekampagnen mit. Du musst nicht alles selbst umsetzen können – aber du solltest verstehen, wie gute Projekte in diesen Bereichen geplant und realisiert werden.
Organisationstalent: Du kannst mehrere Kundenprojekte gleichzeitig steuern, Prioritäten setzen und verlierst auch dann nicht den Überblick, wenn an einem Tag fünf Dinge gleichzeitig passieren.
Stressresistenz: Wenn es turbulent wird, wirst du nicht hektisch, sondern fokussiert. Du kannst mit Zeitdruck, kurzfristigen Änderungen und intensiveren Projektphasen umgehen und läufst dann eher zur Höchstform auf, als den Überblick zu verlieren.
Kommunikationsstärke: Eine klare, professionelle und zielführende Kommunikation – schriftlich wie mündlich – setzen wir voraus. Du kannst sowohl souverän mit Kunden kommunizieren als auch intern klare Briefings und Aufgaben formulieren.
Eigenverantwortung: Du wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jemand jeden nächsten Schritt vorgibt. Du erkennst, was zu tun ist, sprichst Probleme frühzeitig an und übernimmst Verantwortung für deine Projekte.
Interesse an Marketing & Medien: Social Media, Marketing, Medien und digitale Kommunikation interessieren dich auch über deine unmittelbaren Aufgaben hinaus. Du willst verstehen, welche Plattformen, Formate und Entwicklungen gerade relevant sind.
Offenheit für KI: ChatGPT, Claude und andere KI-Tools sind für dich keine Bedrohung, sondern Werkzeuge. Du hast Lust darauf, herauszufinden, wie wir damit bessere Ergebnisse erzielen und effizienter arbeiten können.

Abwechslung statt immer gleicher Projekte: Vom regionalen Mittelständler bis zum Konzern, von Social-Media-Betreuung über Recruitingkampagnen bis zur Videoproduktion: Du arbeitest mit Kunden aus unterschiedlichsten Branchen und an sehr unterschiedlichen Projekten.
Du siehst, was deine Arbeit bewirkt: Unsere Projekte sollen nicht einfach nur gut aussehen. Wir helfen Unternehmen dabei, sichtbarer zu werden, neue Kunden zu erreichen und passende Mitarbeitende zu gewinnen – insbesondere Unternehmen aus unserer Region.
Ein Arbeitsplatz mit Aussicht: Unser Büro befindet sich im Business Tower Nürnberg – in einem der höchsten Büros der Region.
Kurze Wege & flache Hierarchien: Du arbeitest in einem Team mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen und einem nahbaren Führungsteam. Gute Ideen müssen bei uns nicht erst durch fünf Hierarchieebenen.
Moderne Arbeitsweise: Wir arbeiten digital, nutzen moderne Projektmanagement- und KI-Tools und entwickeln unsere internen Prozesse kontinuierlich weiter.
Flexibilität: Flexible Arbeitszeiten gehören für uns genauso dazu wie die notwendige Flexibilität, die ein abwechslungsreicher Agenturalltag manchmal mit sich bringt.
Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten: Wir wachsen als Unternehmen weiter – und damit entstehen auch für dich Möglichkeiten, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und dich fachlich wie persönlich weiterzuentwickeln.

We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.
When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.
Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.
We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day.

As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

The Regulatory team is at the forefront of navigating the complex, fast-moving legal and regulatory landscapes that shape the future of Uber's Mobility and Delivery business lines. Our mission is to ensure seamless compliance, maintain our operational licenses, and proactively manage relationships with local regulators.
As an Associate Program Manager on the West Regulatory Team, you will act as a critical bridge between our legal experts and regional operations. You will ensure that Uber can continue to scale safely, legally, and efficiently across our Western markets.

In this role, you will manage a diverse portfolio of regulatory, legal, and operational projects, including:
Regulatory Inquiry & Investigation Management: Project managing, organizing, and maintaining comprehensive responses to regulatory inquiries, data requests, requests for information, internal reviews, and reporting.
Compliance & Licensing Research: Assisting the legal team with deep-dive research into local statutes, regulations, and city license requirements to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Public Filings & Submissions: Preparing electronic filings and public comments with local regulators.
Certification & Application Oversight: Managing the end-to-end process of obtaining necessary permits.

3+ years of paralegal experience in either big firm or in-house legal department
Experience in researching statutes and/or regulations is essential
B.A./B.S. or paralegal certificate

## Your Purpose ##
The LNG Manager is responsible for inspecting the construction and outfitting of the related LNG equipment and that fitting is done according to international regulation, ship-s contract, technical specifications, and builder standards.

This role is controlling the quality of the materials used, the compliance with regulation and with IGF Code and highlighting any discrepancies within the approved project.

Potential adjustments when minor technical issues are identified by this role, during the construction phase, may be recorded and shared within the Site team and new building division as lesson learnt to be implemented on next projects.

* Ensures that areas under the described discipline are built within the set timescale and in line with the approved technical design, contractual requirements, and functional requisites.
* Follows the installation and outfitting of all LNG equipment and piping maintaining accurate and up to date records of all activities and inspections.
* Attends project meetings and prepares progress reports.
* Ensures that all commissioning activities are held in accordance with the scope and the specifications, are approved by class and relevant authorities such us Flag and USCG representatives.
* Suggests minor adjustments as may be found necessary on site and follows implementation and development of any architectural / technical design change.
* Highlights relevant aspects of the approved design that can be improved for future constructions.
* Involves the Technical Site Specialist(s) during the construction and commissioning phase to ensure that technical accessibility and functionality of equipment is duly verified.
* Highlights relevant aspects of the ship-s design and technical features that might jeopardise the functional requisites and must be improved for the current project or can be improved for future constructions with new building department approval.
* Assists with Plan Approval activities as required.

* Good knowledge of IGF Code.
* Good knowledge of piping, electrical machinery inspection is a plus as she/he may be requested to cooperate with the technical teams for the daily inspections included within the ship-s construction.
* Experience in a leadership position on board LNG vessels or cruise ships with LNG duty might be beneficial.
* Proficiency with the use of Microsoft Office (including Excel, MS Word, MS Project or equivalent and PowerPoint);
* Familiarity with Marine Rules and International Standards and Regulations.
* Ability to review new building specifications and to read and understand a variety of engineering drawings.

You will have the opportunity to influence productivity, quality, efficiency, and operational performance across highly technical aviation environments and see the results of your work first-hand.

* Find opportunities for improvement by analyzing processes, workflows, bottlenecks, waste, and inefficiencies.
* Make things work better by designing and implementing practical Lean solutions that improve productivity, reduce cycle times, and optimize workflows.
* Be close to the action, driving continuous improvement directly on the shopfloor and within operational environments.
* Solve problems together with the people who do the work, partnering with operators, technicians, engineers, supervisors, and other experts.
* Lead improvement workshops and hands-on optimization activities using structured problem-solving and Lean methodologies.
* Improve flow and workplace efficiency through smarter layouts, workstation organization, tooling, standards, and process documentation.
* Use data to drive decisions, monitoring KPIs such as productivity, efficiency, cycle time, and downtime.
* Get to the root of problems, define corrective actions, and make sure improvements are embedded and sustained.

* You hold a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a comparable technical discipline.
* You have professional experience in manufacturing, industrialization, process optimization, lean operations, or continuous improvement within aerospace, aviation, MRO, or another technically demanding industrial environment.
* You have a strong practical understanding of shopfloor operations, production processes, manufacturing workflows, or aircraft maintenance activities.
* You have demonstrated experience analyzing existing processes and implementing measurable improvements in efficiency, productivity, cycle time, quality, or operational performance.
* You bring a hands-on mindset and are comfortable working directly with operational teams to translate analysis into practical, workable solutions.
* You have strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify root causes, prioritize improvement opportunities, and implement sustainable corrective actions.
* You communicate clearly and build effective working relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including operators, technicians, supervisors, engineers, quality specialists, and management.
* You are fluent in English. Additional languages are an advantage in our international working environment.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies or certification is desirable.
* Knowledge of aerospace manufacturing standards, MRO environments, production layout optimization, tooling, workstation design, process standardization, or installation activities is an advantage.
* You are proactive, solution-oriented, service-minded, and able to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.
If you enjoy being close to the operation, solving real challenges, and turning ideas into measurable improvements, this could be the opportunity for you.
